title: Soil microbiome degradation and restoration
bottleneck: Industrial agriculture has degraded soil microbial communities that drive nutrient cycling, disease suppression, and carbon storage, but restoration is blocked by basic ignorance: most soil microbes are undescribed, their ecological roles unknown, and probiotic inoculants usually fail because introduced microbes cannot establish in resident communities. There is no reliable way to diagnose a sick soil microbiome, let alone cure it.
why_it_blocks: Soil microbes underpin the productivity of all terrestrial food systems; degraded microbiomes force ever more fertilizer and pesticide inputs, raising costs and emissions. The knowledge gap means agriculture keeps mining a biological resource it cannot see or manage.
current_state: Metagenomic sequencing is cataloging soil diversity rapidly, and some inoculants work in specific contexts like legume rhizobia. But predictive, generalizable microbiome management for agriculture remains a distant goal.
